_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — page layouts. Adds the disjoint schema key `pageLayout` to the shared `buildiq` register's components.schemas map (key-union merge, no existing schema is touched). A page layout is what a consuming app's detail page shows for one schema, and optionally for one type value of it. Buildiq stores it and serves it through the `buildiq-page-layout` data-provider leaf (ADR-066); the consuming app merges the answer over its own manifest config and renders its manifest unchanged when nothing answers, so an instance without buildiq behaves exactly as before. Resolution is type value first, then schema-wide, then nothing, and a draft never resolves. See openspec/changes/case-page-layout-per-case-type/specs/page-layout-per-type/spec.md, REQ-OBPL-001 through REQ-OBPL-009.

pageLayout.title: Page Layout
pageLayout.description: What a detail page shows for one schema, and optionally for one type value of it: the header, the tabs, the widget grids inside them, the task-list columns and the upload dialog's fields. An administrator arranges it; the owning app renders it through the buildiq-page-layout leaf and falls back to its own manifest when nothing answers, so an instance without buildiq is unchanged. At most one published layout per (targetApp, register, schema, typeProperty, typeValue): two would mean the consumer rendered whichever came back first. V0.3.0 (screen-overrides-as-a-patch-with-fall-through) makes an override a PATCH over the layout it extends, bound to a named audience, pinned to the base it was cut against. A base that moves puts the override in needs-review, tells its maintainer, and serves the base with the override withheld: the page always renders.

x-openregister-audit-trail.description: A layout decides what a handler sees on a case. Every edit and publication is recorded.

targetApp.title: Target App
targetApp.description: The app whose detail page this lays out.

register.title: Register
register.description: The register slug of the object.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: The schema slug of the object.

typeProperty.title: Type Property
typeProperty.description: The property carrying the type value, when this layout is for one type rather than the whole schema.

typeValue.title: Type Value
typeValue.description: The type value this layout is for. Empty means the layout is the schema-wide one, which is what a type with no layout of its own falls back to.

header.description: The top of the detail page. A type-specific header REPLACES the schema-wide one whole and never merges field by field: merging would leave a page showing four fields an administrator thought they had removed, and nothing would say where they came from (REQ-OBPL-007).

titleField.title: Title Field
titleField.description: The property shown as the page title.

chips.description: Small status markers beside the title.
chips.title: Chips

fields.description: The fields shown in the header, in the order an administrator set.
fields.title: Fields

widgetId.title: Widget Id
widgetId.description: A widget rendered in the header instead of, or beside, the fields.

header.title: Header

tabs.description: The tabs, in the order an administrator set.

id.description: The tab's stable id. This is the key an override patches by, so renaming a tab's label leaves its patches attached and changing its id detaches them on purpose (REQ-OBSO-001).
id.title: Id

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What the tab shows: another app's leaf, a grid of widgets, a group of the object's own fields, or a list of related objects.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The leaf id, for a `leaf` tab. A tab of that kind with no ref is refused: it would render an empty panel with no error.

id.title: Id
id.description: The widget to render, as the manifest names it.

config.description: The widget's own configuration, passed through untouched.
config.title: Config

order.title: Order
order.description: Where the widget sits in the grid.

width.title: Width
width.description: How wide the widget is. The four values are the grid; anything else is refused, because a width the grid does not know renders at zero and looks like a widget that failed to load.

conditions.description: When this widget is shown. Evaluated by the leaf against the host object, so a widget whose conditions do not hold is never sent rather than sent and hidden. An empty list always holds.

field.title: Field
field.description: The property on the host object the condition reads.

value.title: Value
value.description: What it is compared against, for the operators that take one.

conditions.title: Conditions

highContrast.title: High Contrast
highContrast.description: Whether the consumer renders the marked variant. Served as declared; it never changes WHICH widgets come back, so a contrast preference cannot silently remove a widget.

fields.description: The field names, for a `fieldGroup` tab.
fields.title: Fields

relatedRegister.title: Related Register
relatedRegister.description: The register of the related objects, for a `relatedList` tab.

relatedSchema.title: Related Schema
relatedSchema.description: The schema of the related objects, for a `relatedList` tab.

tabs.title: Tabs

widgets.description: Widgets shown on the page outside any tab.

id.description: The widget to render, as the manifest names it.

config.description: The widget's own configuration, passed through untouched.

field.description: The property on the host object the condition reads.

value.title: Value
value.description: What it is compared against, for the operators that take one.

conditions.title: Conditions

highContrast.title: High Contrast
highContrast.description: Whether the consumer renders the marked variant. Served as declared; it never changes WHICH widgets come back, so a contrast preference cannot silently remove a widget.

widgets.title: Widgets

taskList.description: What a case type's task list shows and searches on. Buildiq serves this and NEVER reads or writes a task object: the list is the consuming app's, only its shape is administered here (REQ-OBPL-008).

searchFields.description: The fields the list can be searched on, and how.
searchFields.title: Search Fields

taskList.title: Task List

uploadFields.description: What the document upload dialog asks for on this type.

field.title: Field
field.description: The property the upload dialog asks for.

order.title: Order
order.description: Where it sits in the dialog.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: Whether the person uploading may set it, only read it, or never sees it. A hidden field with no default is refused on save, because it can never be filled and the document would be stored missing it (REQ-OBPL-009).

default.title: Default
default.description: What it is set to when the person does not choose.

uploadFields.title: Upload Fields

name.title: Name
name.description: What this layout or override is called, shown wherever one is listed. An administrator asked why a colleague sees different tabs needs a name to point at.

audience.description: Who this layout is for. `everyone` is the plain layout; `group`, `team` and `user` are internal and are never resolvable for a visitor with no account, whatever the consumer asks for; `portal` is the one a visitor may get. An unset audience reads as `everyone`, so every layout stored before this keeps exactly the reach it had (REQ-OBSO-004).

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: Which group, team, portal or user. Absent for `everyone`.

audience.title: Audience

baseRef.title: Base Ref
baseRef.description: The layout this one extends. Empty means it extends the consuming app's own manifest layout, which is the bottom of the fall-through (REQ-OBSO-001).

layoutDelta.description: The patch this override applies, in the keyed-delta shape `diffManifest` produces and `mergeManifestDelta` applies: tabs and widgets keyed by id, `{"$op": "remove"}` for a deletion, `__order` for a reorder. A patch and never a copy: an override that copied its base would be correct the day it was saved and wrong every day after, because a tab added to the base would never reach it (REQ-OBSO-001).
layoutDelta.title: Layout Delta

baseFingerprint.title: Base Fingerprint
baseFingerprint.description: A hash of the base as it stood when the delta was cut. Written by the editor on every save and never by hand. Resolution compares it against the base in hand, because checking that every patch still finds its key is not enough: a base can move in ways a key match cannot see, such as a tab that kept its id and changed its kind (REQ-OBSO-002).

baseCutAt.title: Base Cut At
baseCutAt.description: When the delta was cut against that base.

maintainer.title: Maintainer
maintainer.description: Who is told when this override drifts. An override whose base moved and whose maintainer nobody can name is an override nobody re-cuts.

status.title: Status
status.description: Lifecycle. Only a published layout is ever served; a draft is the administrator's working copy and resolves to nothing. `needs-review` is where a drifted override lands: its patch is kept untouched so a maintainer can re-cut it, and it is not applied in the meantime (REQ-OBSO-003).

draft.label: Draft
draft.description: The administrator's working copy. It resolves to nothing, which is what lets the next version be built where everyone can see it.

needs-review.label: Needs review
needs-review.description: The base this override was cut against has moved. The patch is kept exactly as it was and is NOT applied; the base is served instead and the answer says an override was withheld. A maintainer re-cuts it against the new base in one action.

retired.label: Retired
retired.description: No longer served, kept for the record.

driftDetected.subject: A screen override needs reviewing
driftDetected.message: The layout "{{name}}" was cut against a base that has since changed, so it is not being applied. The page still renders on the base. Open the override to re-cut it.
